From 5b2c7e0ae762fff2b172caf16b2766cc3e1ad859 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Rui Salvaterra <rsalvaterra@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2021 15:30:38 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] ARM: dts: turris-omnia: fix hardware buffer management
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Hardware buffer management has never worked on the Turris Omnia, as the
required MBus window hadn't been reserved. Fix thusly.

Fixes: 018b88eee1a2 ("ARM: dts: turris-omnia: enable HW buffer management")

Signed-off-by: Rui Salvaterra <rsalvaterra@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Marek Behún <kabel@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Klaus Kudielka <klaus.kudielka@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>

diff --git a/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts b/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts
index 646a06420c77..dc80a909ea88 100644
--- a/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts
+++ b/arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts
@@ -32,7 +32,8 @@ soc {
 		ranges = <MBUS_ID(0xf0, 0x01) 0 0xf1000000 0x100000
 			  MBUS_ID(0x01, 0x1d) 0 0xfff00000 0x100000
 			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x19) 0 0xf1100000 0x10000
-			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000>;
+			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000
+			  MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000>;
 
 		internal-regs {
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm/boot/dts/armada-385-turris-omnia.dts`**
   - A new line was added to the `ranges` property within the `soc` node. Specifically, the line:
     ```
     MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000
     ```
     was appended to the existing list of memory bus (MBus) IDs. This addition reserves the required MBus window for hardware buffer management.

### Relationships

- The modification in the device tree source file (`armada-385-turris-omnia.dts`) directly addresses a previously existing issue related to hardware buffer management on the Turris Omnia. The patch references a prior commit (identified by the hash `018b88eee1a2`) that enabled hardware buffer management but did not reserve the necessary MBus window. By adding the new MBus ID, this patch effectively fixes the bug introduced in the earlier commit, ensuring that hardware buffer management can function correctly.

Here is the commit message:
ARM: dts: turris-omnia: fix hardware buffer management
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Hardware buffer management has never worked on the Turris Omnia, as the
required MBus window hadn't been reserved. Fix thusly.

Fixes: 018b88eee1a2 ("ARM: dts: turris-omnia: enable HW buffer management")

Signed-off-by: Rui Salvaterra <rsalvaterra@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Marek Behún <kabel@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Klaus Kudielka <klaus.kudielka@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the lack of a reserved MBus window necessary for hardware buffer management on the Turris Omnia. The previous commit enabled hardware buffer management but did not include the required configuration to allocate the necessary memory bus resources, leading to malfunctioning buffer management.

Here is the patch:

 			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x19) 0 0xf1100000 0x10000
-			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000>;
+			  MBUS_ID(0x09, 0x15) 0 0xf1110000 0x10000
+			  MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000>;

```plaintext

```
Reason:
The absence of a reserved MBus window for hardware buffer management caused the malfunction. The previous configuration only included one MBus ID, which did not allocate the necessary resources for proper buffer management.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```plaintext
MBUS_ID(0x0c, 0x04) 0 0xf1200000 0x100000>;
```
Reason:
Adding the new MBus ID configuration reserves the required memory bus resources, enabling the hardware buffer management to function correctly on the Turris Omnia. This allocation ensures that the necessary memory space is available for the hardware to manage buffers effectively.
